answer: Latency-Bid Admission. Each new identity must submit a bid to delay its own first payout; the protocol sorts bids and grants throughput only to the top tranche, like water rights in an oasis. Winning a slot requires forfeiting the bid's interest to existing members, so an attacker buying N identities pays N escalating delay costs plus forfeited yield. Marginal cost per identity rises with cluster size, making mass registration unprofitable while a single vine can still climb the garden.
